questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'. **

The people of Orleans, while (1)/ they first saw her in their (2)/ city, thought she was an angel. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Part 1 of the given sentence has an error.
 
• **'While' **is used in a sentence when a moment is happening, during. 
 
 
• Ex. *He was watching me while running.*
 
 
 
• **'When' **at or on which (referring to a time or circumstance). 
 
 
• Ex.* I used to do that stuff when I was young. *
 
 
 
• Hence **'when' should be used in place of 'while'**, because the people of Orleans saw her at a particular time.

 

Correct sentence__: '*The people of Orleans, **when** they first saw her in their city, thought she was an angel.'*

questions.question:
Directions: Each of the following sentences in this section has a blank space and is followed by four choices. Select the most appropriate choice to fill in the blank and mark your response accordingly.** **

The sniper was able to ________ two rebels.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** Shoot down.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Shoot down** is a **phrasal verb** **of Shoot which means to** kill or wound someone by shooting them, especially in a ruthless way.

 
 
• ​Ex. *Police had to **shoot** him **down,** because of the threat he posed. *
 
 
 
• **Shot - **The firing of a gun or cannon.
 
 
• Ex. *Anup killed him with a single shot*
 
 
 
• **Shoot of** is not a word.
 
• Hoot with is not a word, 
 
 
• ​Hoot - to shout or laugh usually derisively 
 
 
• Ex.* T**he audience broke into hoots of laughter*
 
 
 
 
 
• Hence, **'shoot down'** should be used in the given space. 

 

**Correct sentence**__**:* '****The sniper was able to **shoot down **two rebels.'*

**In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the one which is opposite in meaning of the given word. **

Progress
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Retreat.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Progress - onward, the forward movement towards a destination. 

 
 
• Synonyms - Development, advance, progression. 

 
 
• Ex. *The road work is in progress. *
 
 
 
 
 
• Retreat - Move back, withdraw. 
 
 
• Ex.* you got to retreat the force. *
 
 
 
• Hence, opposite of 'progress' will be 'retreat'. 
 
• 'Gain', 'march' and 'rise' are the synonyms of 'progress'.

questions.question:
**Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order. **

Of Homer’s two

P : has always been more

Q : epic poems, the Odyssey

R : popular than the Iliad
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** QPR.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• 'Two' quantity must be followed by a noun. Only Q qualifies (**epic poems**) as the next part of the sentence. 
 
• As the sentence tries to compare the epic poems, more *(has always been **more***) is followed by than (*popular **than** the Iliad)*. 
 
• Hence the correct order is QPR. 

 

**Correct sentence__:** '*Of Homer's two epic poems, the Odyssey has always been more popular than the Iliad.'*

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect Speech. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct Speech. **

Anjali said, “I eat two guavas.”

options.text: Anjali say she eat two guavas.
Two guavas are eaten by Anjali.
Anjali said that she ate two guavas.

questions.solution: I eat = simple present tense. Thus, the reported speech will be in **simple past tense** i.e. *she ate*. Option 3) *Anjali said that she ate two guavas *is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph. **

Without entirely

A-them that he would do the

B-dismissing their case, he assured

C-needful that night itself
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** BAC.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece41860
95afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Entirely - fully. It is an adverb and therefore, must be followed by a verb. **Only B (*dismissing) *qualifies this criterion. B is first.
 
• Part B is followed by A as the person is assuring others (them) should be followed. 
 
• Statement C will be the last part. 
 
• Thus, Option 2) *BAC *is the correct answer.

 

**Correct sentence:__** *Without entirely dismissing their case, he assured them that he would do the needful that night itself.*
